hero.title: Low Compression UK Causes, Repair Costs & Diagnostic Guide
hero.description: Low compression doesn't automatically mean a full rebuild. A compression test and leak-down test tell you exactly where pressure escapes - valves, rings, or head gasket. Each has a very different cost. Proper diagnosis first saves you from paying for work you don't need.

ordered.title: Don't ignore these warning signs
ordered.description: Low compression manifests in progressive drivability issues. Identifying them early prevents total engine breakdown.

cards.text: Hard starting - cranks 3-5 seconds before firing, especially cold Rough idle - engine shakes when stationary Misfire - intermittent or constant (fault code P030X) Loss of power - sluggish uphill or under load Poor fuel economy - 15-30% drop in MPG
items: Hard starting - cranks 3-5 seconds before firing, especially cold
Rough idle - engine shakes when stationary
Misfire - intermittent or constant (fault code P030X)
Loss of power - sluggish uphill or under load
Poor fuel economy - 15-30% drop in MPG

blocks.text: 🚨 Critical: Low compression on one cylinder often allows running (badly). Low compression on two adjacent cylinders usually means head gasket failure between them. Low compression on all cylinders means the engine is worn out - replacement or rebuild is the only answer.

ordered.title: Compression test & leak-down test
ordered.description: A proper diagnosis requires two tests. Compression test tells you that compression is low. Leak-down test tells you where it's going.

cards.title: Step 1: Compression Test (£80 - £150)
cards.text: Mechanic removes spark plugs (petrol) or glow plugs (diesel) and screws a gauge into each cylinder.
cards.fullText: Step 1: Compression Test (£80 - £150) Mechanic removes spark plugs (petrol) or glow plugs (diesel) and screws a gauge into each cylinder. Result Meaning One cylinder significantly lower Localised problem - burnt valve, broken ring, head gasket Two adjacent cylinders low Head gasket failure between cylinders All cylinders evenly low General engine wear - worn rings and bores Improves with oil (wet test) Worn rings are the problem Does NOT improve with oil Valve or head gasket issue

cards.title: Step 2: Leak-Down Test (£150 - £250)
cards.text: Pressurised air applied to each cylinder. Listening for where air escapes identifies the exact leak source.
cards.fullText: Step 2: Leak-Down Test (£150 - £250) Pressurised air applied to each cylinder. Listening for where air escapes identifies the exact leak source. Air Escaping From The Problem Oil filler cap or dipstick Worn piston rings Exhaust pipe Burnt exhaust valve Intake manifold Burnt intake valve Coolant expansion tank Blown head gasket or cracked head Adjacent cylinder Head gasket between cylinders

blocks.text: Specialist rule of thumb: "A compression test without a leak-down test is only half the story. Any competent specialist will do both. If a garage quotes a rebuild based only on a compression test, get a second opinion."

ordered.title: What should you do?
ordered.description: Compare repair options against vehicle market value before committing to expensive labour.

rows: Replacement often cheaper on common engines

blocks.text: Engine rebuild vs replacement: On common engines (Ford DV6, VW EA189, BMW N47, Vauxhall Z19DTH), a reconditioned engine is often cheaper than a full rebuild. Compare both.

Vehicle Value Threshold: Under £2,000 - Simple repairs only. If rings or rebuild needed, consider scrap. £2,000-£4,000 - Valve job or head gasket viable. Piston rings: Evaluate carefully. £4,000-£8,000 - Piston rings or full rebuild justified. £8,000+ - Any repair - even full engine replacement.

ordered.title: How bad can it get?
ordered.description: Ignoring low compression symptoms causes cascading damage across exhaust catalysts and bearings.

blocks.text: Ignored early signs - one cylinder slightly low
Driven with misfire (weeks) - cat/DPF damage from unburnt fuel
Driven with low oil pressure (worn rings) - bearing damage
Complete loss of compression - engine won't start

The maths: Diagnose now: £100-£200. Fix now (valve job): £800-£2,000. Ignore and drive (cat/DPF damage): £1,000-£3,500 + original repair. Wait until engine fails to start: £2,500-£6,500 (engine replacement).

ordered.title: Avoiding low compression
ordered.description: Essential maintenance schedules to protect cylinder seal integrity and valve seating.

blocks.text: Specialist rule of thumb: "On an interference engine (most modern engines), timing belt or chain failure means bent valves. Bent valves mean an £800-£2,500 valve job. Replace your timing belt on schedule - it's cheap insurance against a destroyed top end."

blocks.question: What causes low compression? +
blocks.answer: Most common: burnt or bent valves (timing failure or high mileage), worn piston rings (high mileage, poor maintenance), blown head gasket (overheating), worn cylinder bores, or cracked cylinder head.

blocks.question: How do I know if my engine has low compression? +
blocks.answer: Symptoms: hard starting (especially cold), rough idle, misfire, loss of power, poor fuel economy, failed MOT emissions. The only definitive test is a compression test (£80-£150).

blocks.question: What is the difference between a compression test and a leak-down test? +
blocks.answer: Compression test measures maximum pressure - tells you that compression is low. Leak-down test applies pressurised air and listens for escape - tells you where (valves, rings, or head gasket).

blocks.question: Is low compression on one cylinder worth fixing? +
blocks.answer: Yes, if vehicle worth £2,500+. A valve job (£800-£2,000) or head gasket (£550-£1,200) is often economical. If worn rings on a high-mileage engine, a full rebuild (£1,500-£3,500) may be required - evaluate vehicle value.

blocks.question: Is it better to rebuild or replace the engine? +
blocks.answer: On common engines (Ford DV6, VW EA189, BMW N47), a reconditioned engine is often cheaper than a rebuild. A rebuild uses new parts and may last longer. A used engine is a gamble on its history. Discuss with your specialist.

blocks.question: Which engines have the most low compression problems? +
